forces.title: B2B commerce friction constrains MSME credit access
forces.description: Despite digital payment penetration, B2B commerce suffers from information asymmetry and manual operations. This creates inefficiency in B2B workflows, leading to underserved thin-file SME borrowers and a significant credit gap of over INR 60 lakh crore, with formal channels meeting only 30-40% of debt demand for smaller enterprises. This is a critical barrier for NBFCs' MSME lending capabilities, as fragmented data hinders accurate assessment and efficient capital deployment.
forces.source_title: India’s Next Growth Frontier: B2B Commerce, Payments, and Credit

forces.title: Interoperable layer to unify B2B transaction data
forces.description: A centralized, interoperable digital layer is proposed to connect entities and digitize the entire order-to-cash cycle in B2B commerce. This secure information exchange rail, linking business systems and transacting banks via standardized APIs, aims to reduce information asymmetry, strengthen supply chain resilience, improve access to working capital, and support more informed credit decisions for MSMEs. This structural change provides a foundational enhancement for NBFCs to streamline B2B lending and risk assessment.
forces.source_title: India’s Next Growth Frontier: B2B Commerce, Payments, and Credit

forces.title: Digital infrastructure supports MSME credit access
forces.description: Platforms like TReDS, OCEN, and ULI are part of India's growing digital infrastructure, specifically designed to help MSMEs access working capital more quickly, deliver embedded credit, and enable faster, more accurate lending decisions through verified data sharing. These initiatives provide a strong tailwind for NBFCs focused on MSME financing by streamlining processes, reducing information asymmetry, and creating new avenues for product innovation and market penetration in the critical MSME segment.
forces.source_title: India’s Next Growth Frontier: B2B Commerce, Payments, and Credit

forces.title: Cash-flow-based lending emerging for underserved MSMEs
forces.description: Traditional collateral-based underwriting is often unfeasible for many MSMEs, leading to a significant credit gap. Cash-flow-based lending is emerging as an alternative, shifting risk assessment from assets to live business activity. This approach enables credit access for thin-file and credit-invisible MSMEs, offering a structural opportunity for NBFCs to penetrate this underserved segment, provided unified digital transaction data becomes available. This fundamentally alters how NBFIs can assess and extend credit to a key growth demographic.
forces.source_title: India’s Next Growth Frontier: B2B Commerce, Payments, and Credit

forces.title: MSMEs face severe working capital constraints and high informal credit costs
forces.description: MSMEs have INR ~8.1 lakh crore in receivables locked by delayed payments, with over 52% of B2B payments overdue for more than 90 days. This increases their cash conversion cycle by 10+ days and is a major factor in MSME mortality (60%+). Forced reliance on informal credit at 30-60% p.a. severely compresses margins, posing a significant risk for MSMEs. This highlights an urgent need for formal, affordable credit, which NBFCs are uniquely positioned to provide, but the underlying payment delays present a systemic challenge for their clients.
forces.source_title: India’s Next Growth Frontier: B2B Commerce, Payments, and Credit

forces.title: Unified B2B digital layer to boost affordable MSME credit
forces.description: The proposed central interoperable layer, by providing standardized, verified, and auto-matching transaction records (POs, GRNs, invoices, payments), shifts MSME underwriting from collateral to cash flow. This reduces risk premiums, expands formal credit access to credit-invisible MSMEs, frees up working capital via receivables financing, and enables economical small-ticket, transaction-based lending. This is a powerful upside driver for NBFCs in the MSME finance space, facilitating deeper penetration and more robust, diversified lending portfolios.
forces.source_title: India’s Next Growth Frontier: B2B Commerce, Payments, and Credit

forces.title: India's DPI to enable intelligent financial operating systems
forces.description: India's digital public infrastructure (Aadhaar, UPI, Account Aggregator, ULI) is foundational for the next era of financial services, moving beyond mere digitization to intelligent financial operating systems. This environment, where AI, trusted data, programmable money, and DPI converge, will enable autonomous, resilient, and inclusive financial services, providing a structural tailwind for all financial institutions, including NBFIs, by enhancing efficiency, expanding reach, and fostering innovation in product delivery and risk management.

forces.title: DPI enables AI-driven underwriting and financial inclusion for NBFIs
forces.description: India's Digital Public Infrastructure (UPI, Aadhaar, Account Aggregator) creates a rich real-time financial data ecosystem. This foundation enables AI-driven underwriting, financial inclusion, and hyper-personalized financial services at scale. For NBFIs, this represents a significant upside driver, allowing them to leverage advanced analytics for more efficient risk assessment and broader outreach to underserved segments, fostering growth in areas like microfinance and consumer lending while potentially improving asset quality.
forces.source_title: Beyond automation: How AI is reshaping the next decade of banking

forces.title: AA and ULI to revolutionize credit decisions
forces.description: The Account Aggregator framework and Unified Lending Interface (ULI) are poised to make verified financial information portable and credit decisions significantly more contextual. This shift moves finance from isolated transactions to coordinated outcomes. For NBFIs, this structural change provides access to rich, consent-based borrower data, enabling more precise risk assessment, faster loan origination, and the development of innovative, personalized credit products, especially for segments previously underserved due to lack of traditional data, such as MSMEs and rural customers.

forces.title: Rising AI-driven cyber threats for financial institution security
forces.description: The emergence of generative AI (GenAI) and deepfakes significantly widens the attack surface for financial institutions, allowing for convincing phishing campaigns, automated vulnerability hunts, and social engineering at scale. Regulators in India have specifically warned about deepfakes compromising digital financial systems. This escalating cyber threat poses a high key risk for NBFIs, demanding significant investment in cybersecurity, data sovereignty, robust governance, and continuous model updates to protect against fraud, maintain trust, and comply with evolving regulatory expectations.
forces.source_title: Beyond automation: How AI is reshaping the next decade of banking

forces.title: RBI establishes unified cybersecurity and tech risk framework for NBFCs
forces.description: The RBI issued comprehensive "Cybersecurity, Technology: Risk, Resilience and Assurance Framework Directions" on July 31, 2026, establishing a unified framework for technology governance, cybersecurity, operational resilience, and information systems assurance. These directions apply to NBFCs, among other regulated entities, covering roles of the Board, 31 baseline control domains, continuous monitoring, third-party risk, and IS Audit. This represents a significant structural change imposing higher compliance burdens and requiring substantial investment in technology and security infrastructure for NBFCs, potentially impacting their operational costs and agility.
forces.source_title: RBI’s technology focused master directions issued on 31 July 2026

forces.title: RBI mandates enhanced digital payment security for credit card NBFCs
forces.description: The RBI issued "Digital Payment Security Controls Directions" on July 31, 2026, establishing a comprehensive security framework for digital payment channels. These directions specifically apply to Credit Card Issuing NBFCs, requiring board-approved policies for digital payment products/services, channel-specific security chapters (internet banking, mobile payments, cards), and enhanced fraud risk management/reconciliation mechanisms. This imposes significant new compliance and investment requirements on relevant NBFCs, enhancing security but also increasing operational complexity and costs for this specific segment of the NBFI sector.
forces.source_title: RBI’s technology focused master directions issued on 31 July 2026

forces.title: AI-powered agents to expand credit access for consumers and MSMEs
forces.description: The shift towards an intelligent financial ecosystem, driven by AI-powered agents, is expected to expand access to credit for both consumers and small and medium enterprises (MSMEs). These agents will facilitate seamless financial management, risk assessment, and commerce. This represents a significant upside driver for NBFIs (IN070201) as it enables minimal-friction credit origination, automated cash flow management, and improved risk assessment for previously underserved segments, fostering broader financial inclusion and growth for NBFIs leveraging these technologies.

forces.title: Open finance and data ecosystems boost NBFI innovation
forces.description: The expansion of open finance and customer-owned data ecosystems, characterized by consent-based data portability and interoperable frameworks, is accelerating ecosystem-led innovation. This trend enables data-driven services and new business models across financial services. For NBFIs (IN070201), this serves as a strong tailwind, providing access to richer customer data for enhanced underwriting, personalized product offerings, and more efficient risk management, thereby fostering competitiveness and growth in areas like consumer and MSME finance.

forces.title: Deepening linkages across financial institutions
forces.description: The financial system is experiencing increasing interconnectedness, marked by deepening linkages between banks, non-bank financial institutions (NBFIs), and private markets. Expanding private credit markets and rising retail participation are driving greater focus on transparency, oversight, and financial stability. This structural change means NBFIs (IN070201) will operate within a more integrated ecosystem, potentially leading to new partnership opportunities and funding sources, but also increased regulatory scrutiny and demands for greater transparency and robust risk management practices as systemic risks become more pronounced.

forces.title: Governed agentic AI to automate risk operations
forces.description: Financial institutions are moving towards deploying bounded AI agents for autonomous risk operations, including fraud case-building, AML monitoring, transaction surveillance, and credit underwriting. Regulatory focus is shifting to agent governance, emphasizing action traceability, escalation protocols, and accountability for autonomous decisions. This structural change will transform risk management for NBFIs (IN070201), potentially improving efficiency and accuracy in lending decisions, but also requiring robust AI governance frameworks and significant investment in technology and compliance to manage the associated risks effectively.

forces.title: AI-powered alternative credit assessment for MSMEs
forces.description: AI models are enabling lenders to assess MSME creditworthiness using alternative data like GST filings, utility payments, digital footprints, and e-commerce transactions. This approach has the potential to unlock a USD 130-170 billion credit opportunity by improving access for MSMEs and reducing reliance on informal lending. Emerging AI agents can autonomously assess borrowers and recommend financing options, providing a significant upside driver for NBFIs (IN070201) to expand their lending portfolios and improve risk-adjusted returns in this segment.

forces.title: NBFCs lead record IPO fundraising in financial services
forces.description: India's financial services sector, significantly driven by Non-Bank Financial Companies (NBFCs), achieved a record IPO year in 2025, raising approximately INR 1.95 lakh crore (USD 22.55 billion) across 365 IPOs. This trend, with a robust pipeline of over INR 4 lakh crore for 2026, reflects strong investor confidence in the sector. This serves as a major tailwind for NBFIs, enabling access to capital for growth and expansion, and demonstrating market appetite for their business models, which can support further leverage and balance sheet growth.

forces.title: NBFCs poised to lead financial sector profit growth
forces.description: India's financial services sector is projected to nearly double its profits by FY30, with Non-Bank Financial Companies (NBFCs) specifically highlighted as leading this growth at an anticipated annual rate of 16%. This strong forecast indicates a significant tailwind for the NBFC sector, driven by increasing demand for retail credit, wealth management, and payment services. This positions NBFCs as key drivers of overall financial sector expansion and profitability, attracting further investment and talent into the diversified financial services space.

viewpoints.title: Data-driven trust to unlock MSME credit access
viewpoints.description: Sunil Kamath of Axis Bank states that the future of business financing lies in transforming data into trust. He believes that as digital ecosystems become more interconnected, access to verified transaction and trade data can address historical information gaps that constrained MSME credit. A neutral, interoperable infrastructure will strengthen underwriting, expand access to formal finance, unlock growth capital, and accelerate inclusive economic growth for MSMEs, which directly benefits NBFCs in this segment.
viewpoints.source_title: India’s Next Growth Frontier: B2B Commerce, Payments, and Credit

viewpoints.title: AI-driven systems vital for MSME financial inclusion, trust paramount
viewpoints.description: Gautam Aggarwal of Mastercard highlights India's financial ecosystem at an inflection point, with AI's evolution to agentic systems impacting consumers and businesses. He stresses that securing this digital architecture directly enables economic inclusion for consumers and millions of MSMEs. Innovation must be bounded by transparency, consent, accountability, and security, with trust being the ultimate differentiator. This is a positive outlook for NBFIs focusing on MSMEs, emphasizing the need for robust, trustworthy AI adoption for growth and inclusion.

viewpoints.title: Fintech market gaining momentum, AI driving new opportunities
viewpoints.description: Karim Haji, Global Head of Financial Services at KPMG International, notes that despite current investment being concentrated on large, high-quality deals, the broader fintech market is gaining momentum. He highlights AI as a driver of new opportunities, increased corporate activity, and PE interest in consolidation. This suggests a positive long-term outlook for the fintech sector, which includes many digital-first NBFCs and consumer finance players, pointing to strong growth potential and strategic investment.

viewpoints.title: Strong fintech unicorn pipeline, AI-native startups attracting investment
viewpoints.description: Anton Ruddenklau of KPMG highlights robust investment in early-stage fintech deals and a strong crop of new unicorns in H1'26, including India's KreditBee. He notes that investors are backing high-quality nascent startups, particularly in digital assets, data management, analytics, and core infrastructure, with many being AI-native. This is a positive indicator for the NBFI sector, especially digital lending and consumer finance players (IN070201) that can leverage these investment trends and technological advancements to scale and innovate.

viewpoints.title: Fast-growing sector to build inclusive, intelligent financial architecture
viewpoints.description: Dr. K. Paul Thomas, MD & CEO of ESAF Small Finance Bank, expresses a positive outlook for India's financial sector, which he sees moving towards an intelligent, sovereign, and scalable financial operating system. He emphasizes the exceptional chance for this fast-growing sector to create a truly inclusive financial services architecture. Success will depend on combining intelligence with responsibility, scale with resilience, and technological advancement with customer trust, indicating a clear direction for NBFIs and microfinance players to leverage innovation for broader financial inclusion.

More than 70% of the identified credit gap represents short-term working capital demand for MSMEs.

The high cost of informal credit (30-60% p.a.) creates demand for more affordable formal financing solutions like invoice discounting.

Investors prioritize fintechs that can drive operational efficiencies and achieve significant scale, particularly those with proven business models.

Increasing availability of digital footprints, GST filings, utility payments, and e-commerce transaction data enables new credit assessment models.

Overall positive growth in India's financial services sector provides a conducive environment for NBFC expansion.

demand_drivers.description: Increasing demand for credit from individual consumers continues to drive business for NBFCs.
Expanding opportunities in wealth management and payment services contribute to NBFC sector growth.

pnl_drivers.description: Increased lending volumes, particularly in retail credit, drive higher interest income and fee-based revenue.
Adoption of digital-first strategies and technology helps improve cost-to-income ratios and boost profitability.

Users can carry their verified financial histories across various lenders and financial service providers, eliminating the need to rebuild credit profiles.

Access to richer data enables NBFIs to develop highly tailored and personalized lending and financial services.
